headline: HOW TO STOP CHASING CLIENTS FOR THE LAST PAYMENT
first_sentence: The job is done, the client loves it, and the last payment is stuck behind a string of excuses and a phone that goes straight to voicemail.

headline: GETTING PAID IS DECIDED WHEN THE CONTRACT IS SIGNED
first_sentence: It feels like the fight over the last payment starts on the final day of the job, but it was settled long before that, the day you and the client signed the paper.

headline: TIE EVERY PAYMENT TO FINISHED WORK
first_sentence: There is a way to set up a job so you are not waiting on most of the money at the very end, and it has nothing to do with a bigger deposit.

headline: NO EXTRA WORK WITHOUT A SIGNED CHANGE ORDER
first_sentence: The client walks out onto the half-built deck and asks, "While you're here, can you add a step down to the patio?"

headline: WRITE THE PAYMENT SCHEDULE BEFORE THE WORK STARTS
first_sentence: Before the first board is cut, a single page decides whether the last payment shows up when it should or turns into a string of reminder texts.

headline: WHY THE LAST PAYMENT STALLS AFTER THE JOB IS DONE
first_sentence: The moment the last board goes up, the client has everything they hired you to build, and you have a bill they can pay whenever they feel like it.

headline: WHAT THE VIRAL FENCE TEARDOWN TEACHES ABOUT GETTING PAID
first_sentence: On September 13, 2026, a fence crew in Joliet, Illinois posted video of themselves pulling out a fence they had just put in, saying the homeowner refused to pay.

headline: HOW TO GET PAID WITHOUT TEARING OUT YOUR WORK
first_sentence: What do you do when the job is finished, the client won't pay, and the only move you can think of is taking your work back?

headline: YOUR CONTRACT DECIDES IF YOU GET THE LAST PAYMENT
first_sentence: When a client stops answering about the last payment, what do you actually have in writing that says they owe it, and when?

headline: WHAT TO PUT IN YOUR CONTRACT SO YOU GET PAID
first_sentence: Pull out the last contract you signed and look for when each payment is due, what finished work it's tied to, and what happens when the client asks for something extra.

headline: THE PAPER TRAIL THAT GETS YOU PAID
first_sentence: Ask a lawyer whether you can sue a homeowner who won't pay, and the answer starts with what you can prove: the contract, the photos and the texts.

headline: DON'T LET THE CLIENT DECIDE WHEN YOU GET PAID
first_sentence: If your paperwork just says "balance due on completion," the client gets to decide what completion means and when it happened.

headline: A BIGGER DEPOSIT WON'T PROTECT YOUR LAST PAYMENT
first_sentence: Taking more money up front sounds like the fix, but California caps down payments on home improvement jobs, and a big deposit does nothing for the money you're owed at the end.

headline: UNSIGNED CHANGE ORDERS PUT YOUR LAST PAYMENT AT RISK
first_sentence: Plenty of fights over the final payment don't start at the end of the job at all; they start in the middle, with a quick yes to extra work that nobody wrote down.

headline: TIRED OF CHASING THE LAST PAYMENT? START WITH THE CONTRACT
first_sentence: How many times have you finished a job and then spent weeks sending polite texts about the money?

headline: YOU FINISHED THE JOB. WHY ARE YOU STILL CHASING MONEY?
first_sentence: After ten years in deck and rail, we know when a job turns risky: the day the last board goes up and the client already has everything they wanted.

headline: WHEN CLIENT CASH GETS TIGHT, PROTECT YOUR FINAL PAYMENT
first_sentence: On September 16, 2026, the Federal Reserve raised rates to 3.75–4%, so here is a fair question for any owner with jobs on the board: when a client's money gets tight, which payment do they hold back first?

headline: GETTING PAID STARTS BEFORE THE WORK DOES
first_sentence: The best time to settle the last payment is at the kitchen table, before anyone picks up a tool, while you and the client are both still excited about the job.

headline: MAKE THE MONEY MOVE AS THE WORK GETS DONE
first_sentence: Picture a job where the client pays as each stage is finished, so by the time you pack up the truck, only the last small piece is left to collect.

headline: HOW TO WRITE A PAYMENT SCHEDULE TIED TO FINISHED WORK
first_sentence: California's state licensing board requires a home improvement payment schedule to spell out each phase of the work and the payment tied to it, and that rule is a good model even if you never work there.

headline: SOME STATES REQUIRE A WRITTEN CONTRACT. EVERY JOB NEEDS ONE
first_sentence: Illinois requires a signed written contract before any home repair or remodeling job over $1,000, and the reason to write one goes well beyond keeping the state happy.

headline: DON'T LEAVE THE LAST PAYMENT ON A HANDSHAKE
first_sentence: A handshake feels like trust on the first day of a job, but on the last day it is just your word against the client's.

headline: HOW SMALL CREWS PROTECT THE MONEY BEFORE THE JOB STARTS
first_sentence: A small crew can do everything right on the build and still come up short on cash if the paper signed before day one never said when the money moves.

headline: TEARING OUT A FENCE IS NOT A PAYMENT PLAN
first_sentence: When a Joliet, Illinois fence crew tore out a fence in September 2026 over a bill the homeowner allegedly refused to pay, the comments split between calling it payback and calling it a legal line crossed.

headline: WHY SMALL CREWS GET STUCK CHASING THE FINAL PAYMENT
first_sentence: Electricians have a long-running thread on the Mike Holt forums about customers who won't pay, which tells you this problem is not about one bad client.
